did_you_know.text: Did you know? The priests, Aaron and his sons, bore a very heavy responsibility: they were required to bear the 'iniquity of the sanctuary' and the 'iniquity of their priesthood' – meaning any fault or flaw in the holy service was attributed to them.

Did you know? The priesthood was given to the priests as a divine 'gift,' but this gift came with immense responsibility and strict prohibitions against an 'unauthorized person' approaching – entering the sanctuary without authority was punishable by death.

Did you know? The priests didn't receive a fixed salary; rather, their portion came from 'My heave offerings' – the sacrifices and contributions brought by the Israelites to God, signifying their complete dependence on Him.

Did you know? Some holy contributions and gifts given to the priests, like 'the heave offering of their gift' (wave offerings), could be eaten not only by the male priests but also by their family members (including their daughters), provided they were ritually pure.

Did you know? The phrase 'all the best (literally 'fat') of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the grain' refers to the finest and highest quality part of these produce, not actual fat. It's an expression emphasizing the importance of giving the very best to God.

Did you know? 'Cherem' (devoted property) was something absolutely and irrevocably dedicated to God, and it usually became the property of the priests. Such dedication sometimes served as a way to honor the sacred or deal with forbidden possessions.

Did you know? The redemption price for a firstborn son, given to the priests, was fixed at five silver shekels (about 57 grams of silver), which was a significant sum at the time and reflected the importance of the firstborn.

Did you know? The 'Covenant of Salt' (ברית מלח עוֹלָם) was an expression for an eternal and unbreakable covenant, as salt was used in ancient times as a preservative and symbolized stability, loyalty, and permanence.

Did you know? The Levites, including the priests, did not receive a share of the land of Israel like the other tribes, because God told Aaron: 'I am your portion and your inheritance.' This emphasized their unique role and complete dependence on Him.

Did you know? The Levites received all the tithes from the Children of Israel as 'payment' for their service in the Tabernacle. In this way, all the tribes supported those who served God exclusively, without needing to work the land.

Did you know? Even the Levites, who received tithes, had to separate a 'tithe of the tithe' from everything they received and give it to the priests. This created a clear hierarchy of holiness and giving even within the tribe of Levi.
